overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The 2014 executive sessions were properly held under Purpose 6, the procedural-statement claim was untimely, and the minutes were released and handled properly. No orders were issued.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly convened two December 2014 executive sessions on real property without a valid statutory purpose, since no negotiating position existed.
allegations.key_passage: Our review of the December 2 and 16, 2014 executive session minutes reveals that the Board discussed the value of the Woodland Acres property, which is clearly within the ambit of Purpose 6.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly gave insufficient statement before entering the 2014 executive sessions and failed to state that open discussion would harm the town's negotiating position.
allegations.key_passage: Because these apparent deficiencies were discoverable during the open session portions of the December 2 and 16, 2014 meetings, any complaints should have been filed within 30 days of each meeting.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to release the 2014 executive session minutes once the purpose for secrecy expired.
allegations.key_passage: As discussed above, we find that the town had an ongoing negotiating position until January 2017, and we therefore find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by waiting until January 17, 2017 to publicly release the minutes.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to provide executive session minutes when an individual requested them.
allegations.key_passage: We further find that the Board appropriately responded to requests for the executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to review its executive session minutes periodically to determine whether they could be released.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board satisfied its obligations under the Open Meeting Law.
